foot: the loop  ·  what is measured  ·  the rule  ·  the forecast  ·  interventions
narration: A I increasingly generates and selects its own training data, through self-rewarding pipelines, constitutional loops, and synthetic data. A model's current behavior therefore helps determine the data that changes it, and a value can persist, weaken, or amplify through training. Alignment work has recognized the reflectivity of values and the resulting feedback dynamics. There is empirical work on whether frontier models defend their values, on degradation under recursive training, and on attractor states that emerge between models. Little of that work follows these dynamics through training and across settings and seeds.

caption: A model's answers become the data that trains its successor
narration: In a judging loop, a model generates candidate answers, then is trained on the ones a judge prefers in pairwise comparisons against alternatives. The breeder's equation, from selection theory, gives three quantities to measure here: variation among the candidates, what the judge favors, and how the model changes through training.

caption: Six candidates per prompt, two kept, train, then re-measure
narration: I fine-tuned two open-weight models with value orientations, one risk-seeking and one insecure-code-generating. Each round an organism writes six candidates per prompt, and a judge compares each against an alternative and keeps the two it prefers as training data. Held-out prompts re-measure the value between rounds. Runs varied the judge, the candidate source, and the alternative source.

caption: Qwen3-4B and OLMo-3-7B, with example answers and their 0-1 scores
narration: An organism's value is the mean value score of its answers, on a zero to one scale. For the gambling organism, the score is the share of answers picking the risky gamble. For the insecure-code organism, it is how insecure its answers to three fixed questions about its own coding habits read, scored by its frozen base model.

caption: Spread and agreement, measured in each prompt's pool and averaged
narration: Spread is the standard deviation of the candidates' value scores within a prompt, averaged over the round's prompts. Agreement is the correlation between the judge's preferences and those value scores. Their product forecasts the gap between the kept answers and the pool average. Across three hundred sixty-seven rounds it reconstructs the realized gaps at R squared zero point eight zero.

caption: The one-round rule: next value = kept candidate value mean
narration: The one-round rule has no fitted coefficient. The next measured value is the mean value score of the two candidates the judge kept. Holding out each complete experimental condition, it predicts the next value with mean absolute error zero point zero eight one across three hundred forty rounds, against zero point one two eight for assuming no change.

caption: The same update, iterated from round one with nothing re-measured
narration: Before selection, the forecast replaces the kept mean with spread times agreement. On matched rounds it predicts the next value at zero point one zero zero, against zero point zero eight five using the actual kept mean. For endpoints, the model repeats that update from the round-one candidate mean, with spread, agreement, and pool composition held fixed.

headline: Endpoint MAE 0.118, against 0.431 for assuming no change
sub: Spread, agreement and pool composition, all measured in round one
narration: That iteration predicts the final value of a run from its first round with a mean absolute error of zero point one one eight on the zero to one value scale, against zero point four three one for assuming no change.

caption: 32 self-only four-round runs: every candidate came from the organism
narration: This figure isolates the thirty-two self-only four-round runs. On that subset the recurrence has endpoint error zero point one five nine, against zero point two six nine for assuming no change. The forecast holds up further out, with error zero point one zero zero one round ahead and zero point one three zero four rounds ahead, while assuming no change degrades from zero point three one to zero point four three.

caption: Where the noise enters, and how each term was sized
narration: The deterministic forecast gives only the average path real runs scatter around. Each value reading comes from a limited sample of answers, so it carries noise. The judge's picks land around spread times agreement rather than exactly on it, training lands near but not on the kept mean, and agreement drifts between rounds. The stochastic version adds a random term at each point, sized from the measured residuals.

caption: One simulated draw per run, against the observed trajectories
narration: The stochastic model reproduces the observed dynamics. Simulated runs accumulate zero point seven zero nine of round-to-round value change against zero point six four eight observed, and change direction one point two two times per run against one point two zero. Endpoints scatter with a standard deviation of zero point three eight seven against zero point three seven zero, and eighty-nine percent of observed final values fall inside the model's eighty percent bands.

caption: Two interventions, aimed at spread and agreement
narration: Both interventions targeted spread and agreement. Adding base-model answers to a collapsed pool restored spread, and the judge's agreement then eroded a value that had been stuck. Swapping the base-model judge for a min-risk oracle, which sets agreement to minus one, reversed a run that had climbed near the top of the scale. Each result is a single experiment.

checks: more model families, larger models, longer runs
DPO, online RL against a learned reward model, constitutional feedback
moral judgment, AI identity, emergent misalignment
closer: The forecast is untested outside these two behaviors and these two model families.
narration: The training setup is two model families, small models, short runs, and filtered supervised fine-tuning. The behaviors are risk preference and insecure-code self-description. Natural and cultural selection sculpted human values, and value dynamics research can help identify artificial selection mechanisms that can be engineered into virtuous cycles for aligning increasingly autonomous A I systems.
